_comment: Community-maintained database of well-known EAX-era games, matched by this script's library scanner and used for the install-time 'Heads up' tips. Contributions welcome via PR — see README.md's 'Contributing to the Known Games Database' section for the rules before adding an entry.

games.name: Baldur's Gate: Enhanced Edition
games.tip: The Enhanced Edition itself runs on a from-scratch OpenAL audio engine (added for its native Linux/macOS ports), not DirectSound3D — DSOAL has nothing to intercept on the default install. GOG's purchase does still include the original 1998 classic release as bonus content, downloadable from the product page's 'Extras' section (marketed as 'Baldur's Gate 1 - Complete'); that copy's DirectSound3D EAX calls are intact, so installing it separately and pointing this script at that install folder via a manual Wine prefix should work normally. It isn't in this library scanner itself, since it has no separate Steam/GOG library entry to detect.

games.name: Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition
games.tip: The Enhanced Edition itself runs on a from-scratch OpenAL audio engine (added for its native Linux/macOS ports), not DirectSound3D — DSOAL has nothing to intercept on the default install. GOG's purchase does still include the original 2000 classic release as bonus content, downloadable from the product page's 'Extras' section (marketed as 'Baldur's Gate 2 - Complete'); that copy's DirectSound3D EAX calls are intact (its EAX 2.0 environmental occlusion historically needed VxD drivers under Windows 9x, per the Vogons Wiki's citation for this title — likely moot under Wine), so installing it separately and pointing this script at that install folder via a manual Wine prefix should work normally. It isn't in this library scanner itself, since it has no separate Steam/GOG library entry to detect.

games.name: Deus Ex
games.tip: Deus Ex defaults to the Galaxy audio driver, which DSOAL can't add reverb to (open upstream bug: kcat/dsoal#79). If EAX sounds silent, try the community 'ALAudio for Deus Ex' mod instead — a separate, native-OpenAL audio path for this Unreal Engine 1 title, set via AudioDevice=ALAudio.ALAudioSubsystem in DeusEx.ini.

games.name: Thief Gold
games.tip: Thief Gold runs on the Dark Engine. Pairing this with TFix (built on the NewDark engine patch) is worth considering for broader compatibility fixes alongside EAX.

games.name: Thief II: The Metal Age
games.tip: Thief II: The Metal Age runs on the Dark Engine. Pairing this with T2Fix (built on the NewDark engine patch) is worth considering for broader compatibility fixes alongside EAX.

games.name: System Shock 2
games.tip: System Shock 2 ships pre-patched with NewDark, which has its own OpenAL Soft 'Hardware Acceleration' option in the in-game Audio menu — a separate native path from this script's DSOAL install. Worth trying if EAX doesn't sound right. The System Shock 2 Community Patch (SCP) is also worth pairing, though it's a general bugfix/polish patch, not an audio-specific one. Note: System Shock 2's GOG listing is the 25th Anniversary Remaster, a different build, so it's deliberately left unmapped here rather than pointed at the wrong game.

games.name: F.E.A.R.
games.tip: If EAX audio drops out during large firefights, try this script's 'Expand Audio Limits' Advanced Compatibility Tweak (256 simultaneous sources, 48kHz) — that's exactly what it's for. A separate, older report (kcat/dsoal#67) described DSOAL failing to load under Wine for one user, but that's not universal — if EAX already works, you likely don't need any advanced tweaks. Uses EAX Unified (eax.dll) rather than native DirectSound3D EAX — pairs with this script's EAX Unified Advanced Compatibility Tweak.

games.name: Half-Life
games.tip: Half-Life's Steam release had A3D and EAX removed from the game code entirely in the January 2013 update, and the 2023 25th Anniversary Update didn't restore them. This isn't a DSOAL problem — the game simply no longer makes those calls, so this script's install has nothing to translate on the current Steam build. For genuine EAX/A3D-style reverb and HRTF, look into MetaAudio instead (github.com/LAGonauta/MetaAudio, requires MetaHookSv). If you still have the original pre-2013 CD/retail release installed outside Steam, that copy's EAX calls are intact — point this script at that install folder via a manual Wine prefix (it isn't in this library scanner, since it has no Steam/GOG entry to detect) and DSOAL should work normally there.

games.name: Grand Theft Auto III
games.tip: Delisted from Steam's storefront (Rockstar replaced it with 2021's separate 'Definitive Edition' remaster, a different engine without DirectSound3D EAX) — but this AppID is still valid for detecting/installing on an existing owned copy. If EAX doesn't engage, this script's Advanced Compatibility Tweaks (COM Registry Injection) may help, as it does for Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas on the same RenderWare-derived engine — not independently confirmed for this title specifically.

games.name: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City
games.tip: Delisted from Steam's storefront (Rockstar replaced it with 2021's separate 'Definitive Edition' remaster, a different engine without DirectSound3D EAX) — but this AppID is still valid for detecting/installing on an existing owned copy. Also supports A3D 2.0 via a manual edit of the settings file, per the Vogons Wiki's citation for this title. If EAX doesn't engage, this script's Advanced Compatibility Tweaks (COM Registry Injection) may help, as it does for Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas on the same RenderWare-derived engine — not independently confirmed for this title specifically.

games.name: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
games.tip: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas needs its DirectSound CLSIDs registered directly in the Wine registry to unlock EAX. Make sure to opt into this script's Advanced Compatibility Tweaks (COM Registry Injection) during install. Uses EAX Unified (eax.dll) rather than native DirectSound3D EAX — pairs with this script's EAX Unified Advanced Compatibility Tweak.

games.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines
games.tip: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines isn't documented (per PCGamingWiki) as having hardware EAX support — its acclaimed sound design is mostly scripted ambience, not DirectSound3D reverb zones. DSOAL may have little to no audible effect here; that's expected, not a bug. The 'List of games with EAX support' community database corroborates this: it lists a separate, earlier game, Vampire: The Masquerade – Redemption (2000), as EAX 1.0/2.0-capable, but does not list Bloodlines at all.

games.name: Thief: Deadly Shadows
games.tip: Thief: Deadly Shadows runs on a modified Dark Engine build. The unofficial 'Sneaky Upgrade' patch (works with both the Steam and GOG releases) fixes a well-documented multi-core CPU issue and other modern-system quirks — worth pairing alongside EAX, similar to TFix/T2Fix for the earlier Thief games. Uses EAX Unified (eax.dll) rather than native DirectSound3D EAX — pairs with this script's EAX Unified Advanced Compatibility Tweak. EAX isn't on by default: in-game, go to Options, scroll to the bottom, and enable 'Audio Hardware Mixing', 'EAX ADVANCED HD', and 'EAX Multiple Environments' (per Creative's own setup guide for the game).

games.name: Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne
games.tip: Uses EAX Unified (eax.dll) rather than native DirectSound3D EAX — pairs with this script's EAX Unified Advanced Compatibility Tweak.

games.name: Star Wars Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast
games.tip: This title's own EAX support is implemented via a bundled OpenAL library rather than DirectSound3D — how that interacts with DSOAL hasn't been independently verified here. Per the same source, EAX support was only added in patch 1.03, so make sure the install is patched to at least that version.

games.name: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy
games.tip: This title's own EAX support is implemented via a bundled OpenAL library rather than DirectSound3D — how that interacts with DSOAL hasn't been independently verified here. Full EAX 4.0 ('Multi-Environment'/'Environment Panning') historically required a separate official patch beyond the base install, per Creative's own writeup — likely already included in the current Steam/GOG build, but worth checking the patch/build version if EAX seems limited to a single reverb zone.

games.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II - The Sith Lords
games.tip: Aspyr's 2015 patch removed EAX/A3D environmental audio from the default Steam and GOG builds (confirmed via PCGamingWiki's talk page and Steam Community reports on app/208580) — installing DSOAL is a functional no-op on the current default build. There is a real fix, unlike Half-Life: on Steam, right-click the game -> Properties -> Betas, and select the 'legacypc' branch to revert to the pre-Aspyr build with EAX intact, then run this script against that install.

games.name: Unreal Tournament: Game of the Year Edition
games.tip: The base install only has basic EAX 1.0/A3D support built into its levels. Full EAX 2.0 reverb/occlusion for the original Deathmatch and Capture the Flag maps needs Creative's separate official 'EAX Library Patch' (three files: uteaxsys.zip, then uteaxdm.zip and uteaxctf.zip), historically mirrored at patches-scrolls.com — verify the mirror is still live and the files intact before installing.

games.name: Unreal Tournament 2004
games.tip: This title's own EAX support is implemented via a bundled OpenAL library rather than DirectSound3D — how that interacts with DSOAL hasn't been independently verified here. If EAX seems inactive, check the in-game Audio settings: Audio Mode should be 'H/W 3D + EAX', with Low Sound Detail, System Driver, and Reverse Stereo all unchecked (per Creative's own setup notes for this game).

games.name: Prey
games.tip: This is the original 2006 Human Head Studios game, not the unrelated 2017 Arkane reboot (a different Steam AppID, 480490). Delisted from Steam's storefront in 2009 after a rights dispute, so it can't be newly purchased there anymore — but this AppID is still valid for detecting/installing on an existing owned copy. This title's own EAX support is implemented via a bundled OpenAL library rather than DirectSound3D — how that interacts with DSOAL hasn't been independently verified here.

games.name: DOOM 3
games.tip: GOG's current 'DOOM 3' listing was renamed from 'DOOM 3: BFG Edition' rather than being a separate classic release — a different build with its own (SDL/OpenAL-based) audio path, not the original DirectSound3D-era version this script targets. Deliberately left unmapped here rather than pointed at the wrong build; the Steam AppID above is the original classic release. This title's own EAX support is implemented via a bundled OpenAL library rather than DirectSound3D — how that interacts with DSOAL hasn't been independently verified here. Per the same source, EAX support was only added in patch 1.3, so make sure the install is patched to at least that version.

games.name: Serious Sam Classic: The First Encounter
Serious Sam Classic: The Second Encounter
Mafia (2002)

games.name: Unreal Gold
games.tip: Delisted from Steam's storefront (Epic pulled the original Unreal-series titles from sale), so it can't be newly purchased there anymore — but this AppID is still valid for detecting/installing on an existing owned copy. The GOG release is the actively available option for new purchases. Unreal (1998) was the first game to ever implement EAX support. If hardware 3D audio doesn't seem to engage, check Unreal.ini for UseSpatial=True, UseReverb=True, and Use3dHardware=True under the audio section — these gate whether the engine attempts hardware-accelerated 3D audio at all (documented in an Aureal A3D context, but the flags are generic to the engine's audio subsystem, not vendor-specific).

games.tip: Like the base game, Opposing Force had EAX removed from the Steam build in the January 2013 update — this isn't a DSOAL problem, the game simply no longer makes those calls on the current Steam build. If you still have the original pre-2013 retail/CD release installed outside Steam, that copy's EAX calls are intact and DSOAL should work normally there.

games.name: Icewind Dale II
games.tip: Not sold on Steam — only available on GOG, as 'Icewind Dale 2 Complete'. Unlike Baldur's Gate, Baldur's Gate II, Icewind Dale, Planescape: Torment, and Neverwinter Nights (all rewritten by Beamdog as OpenAL-native 'Enhanced Editions' with EAX support gone, which is why none of those appear in this database), Icewind Dale II never got that treatment and is still the original DirectSound3D-EAX-era Infinity Engine build.

games.name: Neverwinter Nights 2
games.tip: Steam only sells 2025's 'Enhanced Edition' rewrite (a different, OpenAL-native build) — GOG's 'Neverwinter Nights 2 Complete' is still the original 2006 Obsidian/Electron Engine build with DirectSound3D EAX intact, which is why only a gog_id is set here. For 5.1 surround, set Speaker Type=4 in nwn2.ini.

games.name: Medal of Honor: Allied Assault
games.tip: Not currently sold on Steam — only available on GOG, as the 'War Chest' edition bundling the base game with the Spearhead and Breakthrough expansions.

games.name: Rome: Total War
games.tip: EAX is set via the in-game Options > Sound menu, not on by default — per the Vogons Wiki's own citation for this title.

games.name: Stronghold
games.tip: Not currently sold on Steam (delisted in favor of the 2023 'Definitive Edition' remaster, a different engine without DirectSound3D EAX) — GOG's 'Stronghold HD' is the original 2001 Firefly Studios build with EAX support intact.

games.name: The Witcher
games.tip: Only EAX 4.0 is supported. The game's own readme.rtf ('Known Issues' section) and CD Projekt's forums document EAX/Creative X-Fi Alchemy caveats worth checking if audio isn't right.

games.name: Star Wars: Battlefront II (Classic, 2005)
games.tip: Uses EAX Unified (eax.dll version 4.0.1.0) rather than native DirectSound3D EAX — pairs with this script's EAX Unified Advanced Compatibility Tweak.
